where: Section 2, bullet on reading the answer (and lead)
problem: It says the matrix reaches RREF and 'x_k = b′_k is read straight from the last column'. That holds only when every column has a pivot. If a column is skipped, its entry stays non-zero in the pivot rows, so the pivot unknowns come out as x_k = b′_k minus terms in the free variables — the chapter's own worked example gives x = 3/2 − t/2, not x = 3/2.
fix: Write: 'Each pivot row reads x_k + (coefficients of the free unknowns) = b′_k, so x_k = b′_k when every column has a pivot; if a column has no pivot, move those free-variable terms to the right side. No back substitution is needed either way.'

problem: 'If r = n there is one solution' is missing the consistency condition. An overdetermined inconsistent system, for example rows [1 0 | 0], [0 1 | 0], [0 0 | 1], has r = n = 2 and no solution at all.
fix: 'If the system is consistent and r = n there is exactly one solution; if it is consistent and r < n there are infinitely many, written with parameters t₁, t₂, …; a row [0 0 0 | c] with c ≠ 0 means no solution (1.4 develops this).'

where: Section 3, partial pivoting paragraph, and quiz Q8
problem: It claims that with partial pivoting 'entries do not blow up and rounding error stays small'. The |m| ≤ 1 bound is correct, but entry growth is not ruled out: partial pivoting still allows a growth factor as large as 2^(n−1) for specially built matrices. The chapter's own 'Beyond' section mentions the growth factor, so the two parts disagree in tone.
fix: Say: 'every multiplier satisfies |m| ≤ 1, which keeps entries from growing in most practical systems and keeps rounding error small; the worst-case growth factor can still be as large as 2^(n−1), which is why numerical analysts study it.' Match Q8's answer to this wording.

problem: The question asks for 'the two properties' of RREF, but the answer lists four conditions and still leaves one out: the leading 1 of each row must lie to the right of the leading 1 of the row above (the staircase condition). The question and answer do not match.
fix: Ask: 'State the conditions that define reduced row echelon form.' Answer: '(1) zero rows are at the bottom; (2) the first non-zero entry of each non-zero row is 1, and it lies to the right of the leading 1 of the row above; (3) that leading 1 is the only non-zero entry in its column.'
